scope: Proposition 6.6 (Descent from a small Sylow orbit) of the manuscript “The Blockwise Alperin Weight Conjecture” (preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 202 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 042c7730f058d508), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume Op(J) = 1 and fix a multiset C as in Lemma 6.5. There is a finite Galois extension M/Ks through which the action on TC factors. Let PΓ be a Sylow p-subgroup of Γ = Gal(M/Ks). If a PΓ-orbit has size less than ph, one of its marked covers descends to a finite extension L/Ks satisfying [L : Ks]p < ph , [F : F0]p = [L : Ks]p, F = res(L). (6.7) The descended map Y → X = XL has geometrically connected smooth projective source, degree m, the specified J-action, and all branch indices at the ξi divisible by p.
